ports.name: i_a_size
ports.meaning: TL-UL a_size (log2 of the number of bytes)

ports.name: i_a_address
ports.meaning: TL-UL a_address (byte address; the register offsets of the rv_timer specification are relative to 0)

ports.name: i_a_instr
ports.meaning: 1: the request is an instruction fetch (a_user.instr_type = MuBi4True); 0: a data access (MuBi4False)

ports.name: i_a_intg_flip
ports.meaning: 1: the A-channel integrity sent with the request is corrupted (see 4.2)

ports.name: o_d_intg_err
ports.meaning: Response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong (see 4.3)

ports.name: o_alert_integ_fail
ports.meaning: Signal integrity failure on the alert differential pairs (see 5)

checks.title: No alert signal-integrity failure
checks.behavior: At every rising edge with rst_ni=1, o_alert_integ_fail=0. This includes the whole time after a request with i_a_intg_flip=1.

checks.title: o_alert is a single-cycle pulse per handshake
checks.behavior: If rst_ni=1 and o_alert=1 at rising edge k, then o_alert=0 at rising edge k+1.

checks.title: No spurious alerts, no more pulses than test writes
checks.behavior:
Model state:
- flip_seen: set at the acceptance edge of any request with i_a_intg_flip=1; cleared while rst_ni=0.
- regwen: 1 while rst_ni=0; set to 0 at the D beat with o_d_error=0 of a PutFullData (a_size=2, mask 1111) to 0x000 with i_a_data[31]=0.
- Qualifying write: a PutFullData with a_size=2 and mask 1111 to 0x000 with i_a_data[0]=1, accepted while regwen=1.

While flip_seen=0:
(a) Every rising edge with o_alert=1 lies at or after the acceptance edge of some qualifying write. It also lies no later than 16 edges after that write's D beat, and that D beat had o_d_error=0.
(b) The number of edges with o_alert=1 since the last rst_ni release is never larger than the number of qualifying writes accepted since then.

checks.title: Interrupt output masked by INTR_ENABLE0.IE_0
checks.behavior:
Model ie: ie is 0 while rst_ni=0. At the D beat with o_d_error=0 of a request with intg_flip=0 to 0x100 that is either a PutFullData/PutPartialData with a_size=2 and mask 1111 or a PutPartialData with a_size=0 and mask 0001, ie takes that request's i_a_data[0].

Condition: at rising edge k, rst_ni=1, ie=0, no write to 0x100 is outstanding, and no such write had its D beat at edges k-2 to k.

Required: o_intr_timer_expired=0 at edge k.

The check is disabled from the acceptance of a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 until reset.

checks.title: Latched interrupt falls only after a clearing write or reset
Outputs inactive during reset
checks.behavior: At every rising edge (and at any other sample point) where rst_ni=0: o_d_valid=0, o_alert=0, o_alert_integ_fail=0 and o_intr_timer_expired=0. o_a_ready is not checked.

checks.title: Outputs change only at rising clock edges
checks.behavior: The test bench changes inputs only right after a rising edge of clk_i. For every clock period between rising edges k and k+1 where rst_ni=1 at both edges and does not fall in between, each output keeps one value from just after edge k (once the new inputs are applied) until edge k+1. The outputs checked are o_a_ready, o_d_valid, o_d_opcode, o_d_param, o_d_size, o_d_source, o_d_sink, o_d_data, o_d_error, o_d_intg_err, o_alert, o_alert_integ_fail and o_intr_timer_expired. They are sampled just after edge k and at the falling edge of clk_i.

checks.title: Test-bench host obligations (stimulus self-check)
Every D-channel beat matches exactly one outstanding request
checks.behavior: The checker keeps a set of outstanding requests. A request is added at each rising edge where rst_ni=1, i_a_valid=1 and o_a_ready=1, keyed by i_a_source, and it records i_a_opcode, i_a_size, i_a_address, i_a_mask, i_a_data, i_a_instr and i_a_intg_flip. At each rising edge where rst_ni=1, o_d_valid=1 and i_d_ready=1 (a D beat), exactly one outstanding request has a_source equal to o_d_source and was accepted at this edge or an earlier one. That request is removed. A D beat with no matching outstanding request (an orphan) is a failure. At most one D beat completes per edge. The set is cleared while rst_ni=0. From the acceptance of a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 until rst_ni=0, the check is disabled (D-010).

checks.title: Response opcode and size echo
checks.behavior:
For each D beat that CHK-009 matches to a request R with R.i_a_intg_flip=0, checked at the same rising edge:
- If R.opcode=4 (Get), then o_d_opcode=1 (AccessAckData) and o_d_size=R.a_size.
- If R.opcode is 0 (PutFullData) or 1 (PutPartialData), then o_d_opcode=0 (AccessAck) and o_d_size=R.a_size.
- If R.opcode is not 0, 1 or 4, only o_d_error=1 is required.
- In every D beat of a request with defined opcode, o_d_opcode is 0 or 1.
o_d_param and o_d_sink are not checked. The check is disabled from the acceptance of a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 until reset.

checks.title: d_error value for classified requests
checks.behavior:
This applies to each D beat matched to a request R with intg_flip=0, instr=0 and address<0x200.

o_d_error must be 1 if any of these holds:
(a) R.opcode is not 0, 1 or 4.
(b) R.a_size=3.
(c) R.address is not a multiple of 2^R.a_size.
(d) R.mask has a 1 on a byte lane outside lanes R.address[1:0] to R.address[1:0]+2^R.a_size-1.
(e) R.opcode=0 and R.mask is not 1 on every lane of that range.
(f) R.address with bits [1:0] cleared is not one of 0x000, 0x004, 0x100, 0x104, 0x108, 0x10C, 0x110, 0x114, 0x118, 0x11C.
(g) R.opcode is 0 or 1, R.a_size=0, R.mask=0001, and R.address is one of 0x000, 0x10C, 0x110, 0x114, 0x118, 0x11C.

o_d_error must be 0 if none of (a) to (g) holds and R is one of:
- a Get, PutFullData or PutPartialData with a_size=2 and mask 1111 to a mapped aligned address;
- a PutPartialData with a_size=0 and mask 0001 to 0x004, 0x100, 0x104 or 0x108;
- a Get with a_size 0 or 1, an address aligned to that size and a mask equal to exactly the active lanes, to a mapped address.

All other requests are not checked.

checks.title: D channel holds under back-pressure
checks.behavior: If rst_ni=1, o_d_valid=1 and i_d_ready=0 at rising edge k, and rst_ni=1 at edge k+1, then at edge k+1 o_d_valid=1. Also o_d_opcode, o_d_param, o_d_size, o_d_source, o_d_sink, o_d_data and o_d_error equal their values at edge k. The check is disabled from the acceptance of a request with i_a_intg_flip=1 until reset.

checks.title: Response integrity never fails
checks.behavior: At every rising edge with rst_ni=1, o_d_intg_err=0. This includes edges with o_d_valid=1 and the whole time after a request with i_a_intg_flip=1.

checks.title: ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers one alert per write
checks.behavior: A write of 1 to fatal_fault gives exactly one o_alert pulse within 16 cycles of the D beat. The wo bit and the reserved bits read 0.
checks.stimulus: After reset, idle 50 cycles. Write 0x80000001 to 0x000 (PutFullData, a_size=2, mask 1111; acceptance edge a, D beat r), watch until r+100, then read ALERT_TEST. Repeat 3 times, 100 cycles apart. Next, send 3 writes of 0x80000001, each accepted within 10 cycles of the previous one, and watch until the last D beat + 100. Finally write 0x80000000 and 0xFFFFFFFE, watching 100 cycles after each, and read ALERT_TEST.
checks.expected:
- No o_alert pulse during the idle cycles.
- For each isolated write: o_d_error=0, exactly one o_alert pulse at an edge in [a, r+16], no other pulse up to r+100, and ALERT_TEST reads 0x80000000.
- For the closely spaced burst: between 1 and 3 pulses in total.
- For the 0x80000000 and 0xFFFFFFFE writes: no pulse, and ALERT_TEST reads 0x80000000.
- o_alert_integ_fail=0 throughout.

checks.title: ALERT_TEST.regwen rw0c locks alert testing until reset
checks.behavior: Writing 0 to regwen disables alert testing until reset. Writing 1 cannot set regwen again.
checks.stimulus:
1. After reset, write 0x80000000 to 0x000 and read ALERT_TEST.
2. Write 0x00000000 and read ALERT_TEST.
3. Write 0x80000001, watch 100 cycles, then read ALERT_TEST.
4. Write 0x80000000 and read ALERT_TEST.
5. Assert rst_ni=0 for 5 cycles and release it.
6. Read ALERT_TEST, write 0x80000001 (D beat r), and watch until r+100.
checks.expected:
- Step 1: reads 0x80000000.
- Step 2: o_d_error=0 and reads 0x00000000, with no o_alert pulse.
- Step 3: o_d_error=0, no o_alert pulse within 100 cycles, and reads 0x00000000.
- Step 4: reads 0x00000000.
- Step 6: ALERT_TEST reads 0x80000000, and exactly one o_alert pulse occurs at an edge <= r+16.

checks.title: Command integrity error raises a repeating fatal alert until reset
checks.behavior: A request with corrupted A-channel integrity causes o_alert pulses that start within 16 cycles of acceptance and repeat at least every 32 cycles until rst_ni is asserted.
checks.stimulus:
Run 1:
1. After reset, with i_d_ready=1, send one Get (a_size=2, mask 1111) to 0x104 with i_a_intg_flip=1 (acceptance edge a). Do not wait more than 32 cycles for a response.
2. Keep i_a_valid=0 for 1000 cycles.
3. Assert rst_ni=0 for 5 cycles and release it synchronously.
4. Idle 200 cycles, then read CFG0.
Run 2: the same, with a PutFullData of 0x1 to 0x100 with i_a_intg_flip=1.
checks.expected:
- The first o_alert pulse is at an edge in [a, a+16].
- Every window of 32 consecutive edges after it, up to reset assertion, contains at least one pulse.
- o_alert_integ_fail=0 and o_d_intg_err=0 throughout.
- o_alert=0 while rst_ni=0 and during the 200 cycles after release.
- The CFG0 read returns o_d_error=0 and 0x00010000.
- The response to the corrupted request is not checked.

checks.title: Unmapped offsets return error and change nothing
checks.behavior: Requests to word offsets in 0x000 to 0x1FC that are not mapped get d_error=1 and leave every register unchanged. This includes offsets 0x120 and above, so there are no registers for a second hart or timer.
checks.stimulus: After reset, with i_d_ready=1, go through every 4-byte-aligned offset in 0x000 to 0x1FC other than 0x000, 0x004 and 0x100 to 0x11C. Send each one a Get (a_size=2, mask 1111) and a PutFullData (a_size=2, mask 1111, data 0xFFFFFFFF). Then read all 10 mapped registers.
checks.expected: Every request to an unmapped offset has o_d_error=1, with o_d_opcode=1 for Get and 0 for PutFullData. Afterwards all 10 registers still read the CHK-028 reset values. No o_alert pulse occurs and o_intr_timer_expired stays 0.

checks.title: Byte writes per register width
checks.behavior: Aligned byte writes to registers wider than 8 bits fail and change nothing. Aligned byte writes to byte 0 of the 1-bit registers succeed and take effect.
checks.stimulus:
After reset, send PutPartialData (a_size=0, mask 0001, aligned address):
- 0x10C with data 0x05; 0x110, 0x114, 0x118 and 0x11C with data 0x00; 0x000 with data 0x00000000 and then 0x00000001. Read all of them back.
- 0x100 with data 0x01, then read INTR_ENABLE0.
- 0x108 with data 0x01, then read INTR_STATE0.
- 0x104 with data 0x01, then read INTR_STATE0.
- 0x004 with data 0x01, then read CTRL; then 0x004 with data 0x00, then read CTRL.
checks.expected:
- The byte writes to 0x10C, 0x110, 0x114, 0x118, 0x11C and 0x000 return o_d_error=1. Afterwards CFG0=0x00010000, TIMER_V_LOWER0=TIMER_V_UPPER0=0x0, COMPARE_LOWER0_0=COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0xFFFFFFFF and ALERT_TEST=0x80000000. No o_alert pulse occurs within 100 cycles.
- The byte writes to 0x100, 0x108, 0x104 and 0x004 return o_d_error=0.
- INTR_ENABLE0 reads 0x1.
- INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1 after the INTR_TEST0 byte write (read issued 4 or more cycles after its D beat) and 0x0 after the INTR_STATE0 byte write.
- CTRL reads 0x1 and then 0x0.

checks.title: TL-UL protocol error cases
checks.behavior: Requests with an illegal opcode, size, alignment or mask are answered with d_error=1.
checks.expected: Every listed request gets exactly one response with o_d_error=1. For opcodes 0 and 4, CHK-010 also holds (d_opcode, d_size echo). The final CFG0 read returns o_d_error=0 and 0x00010000.

checks.title: Sub-word reads return the full word
checks.behavior: Aligned sub-word reads return the full register word in byte-lane positions, without error.
checks.stimulus: With CTRL=0, write CFG0=0x00AB0123 and COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0x89ABCDEF. Send Get a_size=0 to 0x10C+k with mask (1<<k) for k=0..3. Send Get a_size=1 to 0x118 with mask 0011 and to 0x11A with mask 1100.
checks.expected: Every response has o_d_error=0, o_d_opcode=1 and o_d_size equal to a_size. o_d_data is 0x00AB0123 for the four CFG0 reads and 0x89ABCDEF for the two COMPARE_LOWER0_0 reads.

checks.title: Instruction-fetch reads
checks.behavior: Gets with i_a_instr=1 are answered and have no side effects. o_d_error is not checked for them (D-011).
checks.stimulus: After reset, with CFG0=0x00030005 and COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0x12345678, send a Get (a_size=2, mask 1111, i_a_instr=1) to each mapped register. Then read every register with i_a_instr=0.
checks.expected: Each instruction fetch gets exactly one response with o_d_source equal to a_source, o_d_size=2 and o_d_opcode=1. o_d_intg_err=0, and there is no o_alert pulse within 50 cycles. The later data reads return the values that were programmed (all other registers at their reset values).

checks.title: Interrupt raised by tick when mtime >= mtimecmp
checks.behavior: IS_0 and o_intr_timer_expired are set when a tick makes mtime reach or pass mtimecmp. They stay set (level, latched) afterwards.
checks.stimulus:
For (P, S, C) in (0,1,20), (3,3,10) and (47,1,2), with m=ceil(C/S):
1. With CTRL=0, write CFG0=(S<<16)|P, TIMER_V_LOWER0=0, TIMER_V_UPPER0=0, COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0, COMPARE_LOWER0_0=C and INTR_ENABLE0=1. Clear INTR_STATE0 by writing 0x1.
2. Write CTRL=1 (acceptance edge a0, D beat t0).
3. Watch for m*(P+1)+50 cycles.
4. Write CTRL=0, then read INTR_STATE0 and TIMER_V_LOWER0.
5. Clear the interrupt by writing COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0xFFFFFFFF before the next case.
checks.expected:
- o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge before a0+(m-1)*(P+1).
- o_intr_timer_expired=1 at some edge no later than t0+(P+5)+(m-1)*(P+1)+6, and it stays 1 until deactivation.
- INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1.
- TIMER_V_LOWER0 >= C and is a multiple of S. For (3,3,10) it is >= 12.

checks.title: Interrupt raised by a compare write while active
checks.behavior: When a register write while active makes the condition true, IS_0 is 1 no later than CFG0.prescale+1+4 cycles after the write's D beat.
checks.stimulus:
1. With CTRL=0, write CFG0=0x00010007 (P=7, S=1), TIMER_V_LOWER0=0, TIMER_V_UPPER0=0, INTR_ENABLE0=1, and leave COMPARE_* at reset.
2. Activate and wait 100 cycles.
3. Write COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0, then COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0x5 (D beat r).
4. Read INTR_STATE0 with acceptance at an edge >= r+12.
checks.expected:
- o_intr_timer_expired=0 until the COMPARE_LOWER0_0 write is accepted.
- o_intr_timer_expired=1 at some edge no later than r+14.
- INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1.

checks.title: Clearing by compare writes; mtime write does not clear
checks.behavior: A write to COMPARE_LOWER0_0 or COMPARE_UPPER0_0 that leaves mtimecmp > mtime clears IS_0 and the interrupt within 4 cycles. If mtime >= mtimecmp still holds after the write, IS_0 is 1 again within 4 cycles. Writing TIMER_V alone does not clear the latched state.
checks.stimulus:
Start from the end state of CHK-023 (active, P=7, IS_0=1, IE_0=1). For each step, r is the D beat of that step's write.
(a) Write COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0x1.
(b) Write COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0x0.
(c) Write COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0xFFFFFFF0.
(d) Write COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0x0.
(e) Write COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0x80 after mtime > 0x100. Write CTRL=0 and wait 20 cycles. Write TIMER_V_LOWER0=0 and TIMER_V_UPPER0=0, read INTR_STATE0, then write COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0x80.
Read INTR_STATE0 at an edge >= r+4 after each compare write.
checks.expected:
(a) and (c): INTR_STATE0 reads 0x0 and o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge from r+4 until the next step.
(b) and (d): INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1 and o_intr_timer_expired=1 at every edge >= r+6 (a dip in between is not checked).
(e) After the TIMER_V writes, INTR_STATE0 still reads 0x1 and o_intr_timer_expired stays 1. After the COMPARE_LOWER0_0 write, INTR_STATE0 reads 0x0 and o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge >= r+4.

checks.title: INTR_STATE0 rw1c and event re-assertion
checks.behavior: Writing 1 to IS_0 clears it. If the event condition still holds while active, IS_0 returns to 1 within 4 cycles. Writing 0 to IS_0 has no effect.
checks.stimulus:
(a) Set up active, P=0, S=1, COMPARE=0x0_00000010, IE_0=1, and wait until o_intr_timer_expired=1. Write INTR_STATE0=0x0 and read it. Write INTR_STATE0=0x1 (D beat r) five times, reading INTR_STATE0 at an edge >= r+4 each time.
(b) Write COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0xFFFFFFFF so the condition is false, then write INTR_TEST0=0x1 so IS_0=1. Write INTR_STATE0=0x1 (D beat r) and read it at an edge >= r+4.
checks.expected:
(a) After the write of 0, INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1 and o_intr_timer_expired stays 1 at every edge. After each write of 1, INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1 and o_intr_timer_expired=1 at every edge >= r+6.
(b) INTR_STATE0 reads 0x0 and o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge >= r+6, for at least 100 cycles.

checks.title: Interrupt enable masking and raw INTR_STATE0
checks.behavior: o_intr_timer_expired equals IS_0 AND IE_0, except in the 2 cycles after either one changes. INTR_STATE0 is not qualified by IE_0.
checks.stimulus: Run the CHK-022 case (0,1,20) with INTR_ENABLE0=0. Then write INTR_ENABLE0=1 (D beat r1), INTR_ENABLE0=0 (D beat r2) and INTR_ENABLE0=1 (D beat r3), reading INTR_STATE0 after each write.
checks.expected:
- o_intr_timer_expired=0 throughout the IE_0=0 run.
- INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1 at any read accepted after t0+(P+5)+19+4.
- o_intr_timer_expired=1 at every edge >= r1+2 until the r2 write is accepted, 0 at every edge >= r2+2 until the r3 write is accepted, and 1 at every edge >= r3+2.
- INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1 after every write.

checks.title: INTR_TEST0 sets the latched state (wo field)
checks.behavior: Writing 1 to INTR_TEST0.T_0 sets IS_0 even when the condition is false. INTR_TEST0 reads 0. Writing 0 has no effect.
checks.stimulus:
After reset (inactive, mtime=0, compare at reset value):
1. Write INTR_ENABLE0=1.
2. Write INTR_TEST0=0x1 (D beat r). Read INTR_STATE0 at an edge >= r+4 and read INTR_TEST0.
3. Write INTR_STATE0=0x1 (D beat r').
4. Write INTR_TEST0=0x0 and read INTR_STATE0.
5. Write INTR_TEST0=0xFFFFFFFF and read INTR_TEST0 and INTR_STATE0.
6. Clear IS_0. Write INTR_ENABLE0=0, write INTR_TEST0=0x1, then read INTR_STATE0.
checks.expected:
After step 2: INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1, INTR_TEST0 reads 0x0, and o_intr_timer_expired=1 at every edge from r+6 for 100 cycles (latched).
After step 3: o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge >= r'+6.
After step 4: INTR_STATE0 reads 0x0.
After step 5: INTR_TEST0 reads 0x0 and INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1.
After step 6: INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1 and o_intr_timer_expired stays 0.

checks.title: Reset values and register map
checks.behavior: After reset, every register reads its documented reset value through a full-word Get at its documented offset.
checks.stimulus: Hold rst_ni=0 for 10 cycles and release it synchronously, keeping i_a_valid=0 in the first cycle after release. Then issue one Get (opcode 4, a_size=2, mask 1111, i_a_instr=0, i_a_intg_flip=0, i_d_ready=1) to each of 0x000, 0x004, 0x100, 0x104, 0x108, 0x10C, 0x110, 0x114, 0x118 and 0x11C, one request at a time.
checks.expected:
Every response has o_d_error=0 and o_d_opcode=1. o_d_data is:
- 0x000: 0x80000000
- 0x004: 0x00000000
- 0x100: 0x00000000
- 0x104: 0x00000000
- 0x108: 0x00000000
- 0x10C: 0x00010000
- 0x110: 0x00000000
- 0x114: 0x00000000
- 0x118: 0xFFFFFFFF
- 0x11C: 0xFFFFFFFF

o_intr_timer_expired=0 and o_alert=0 throughout.

checks.title: rw field access types and reserved bits
checks.behavior: Each rw field stores the written value. Reserved bits read 0 and ignore writes. Full-word writes with mask 1111 succeed for both PutFullData and PutPartialData.
checks.stimulus: With CTRL=0, write CFG0, TIMER_V_LOWER0 (0x110), TIMER_V_UPPER0 (0x114), COMPARE_LOWER0_0 (0x118), COMPARE_UPPER0_0 (0x11C) and INTR_ENABLE0 (0x100). Each register gets the patterns 0xFFFFFFFF, 0x00000000, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0x5A5A5A5A and 8 random values. Use PutFullData (a_size=2, mask 1111) for half the writes and PutPartialData (a_size=2, mask 1111) for the other half, and read the register back with a full-word Get after each write. Then write CTRL with 0xFFFFFFFE, 0xFFFFFFFF and 0x00000000 and read it back after each write. Finish with CTRL=0.
checks.expected:
Every write and read has o_d_error=0. The value read back is:
- CTRL: data & 0x00000001
- INTR_ENABLE0: data & 0x00000001
- CFG0: data & 0x00FF0FFF
- TIMER_V_LOWER0, TIMER_V_UPPER0, COMPARE_LOWER0_0 and COMPARE_UPPER0_0: exactly the data written

checks.title: Asynchronous reset, short reset window, pending response discarded
checks.behavior: Reset is asserted asynchronously and released synchronously. It brings every register back to its reset value even with a 2-cycle window, and it discards a pending response.
checks.stimulus:
(a)
1. Program non-reset values into every rw register, set IE_0=1 and IS_0=1 (o_intr_timer_expired=1), and leave the timer active.
2. Drive rst_ni=0 in the middle of a clock period (between rising edges), hold it for 2 cycles, and release it right after a rising edge, with i_a_valid=0 during reset and the first cycle after.
3. Read all registers. Read TIMER_V_LOWER0 again 50 cycles later.
(b)
1. Send a Get to 0x10C with i_d_ready=0 and wait until o_d_valid=1.
2. Assert rst_ni=0 for 3 cycles and release it.
3. Set i_d_ready=1 and idle 20 cycles.
4. Send a new Get to 0x10C with the same a_source.
checks.expected:
(a) o_intr_timer_expired, o_d_valid and o_alert are 0 before the next rising edge after rst_ni falls and while it stays 0. After release, all registers read the CHK-028 reset values, and TIMER_V_LOWER0 still reads 0 after 50 cycles.
(b) o_d_valid=0 while rst_ni=0, and no D beat occurs in the 20 idle cycles. The new Get gets exactly one response with o_d_error=0 and o_d_data=0x00010000.

checks.title: Tick period, step and counting while active
checks.behavior: While active, mtime increases by CFG0.step once every CFG0.prescale+1 cycles, and stops changing when CTRL.active_0 is cleared.
checks.stimulus:
For each (P, S) in (0,1), (0,0xFF), (1,1), (3,5), (47,1), (0xFFF,0x80) and (10,0):
1. With CTRL=0, write CFG0=(S<<16)|P, TIMER_V_UPPER0=0 and TIMER_V_LOWER0=V0=0x1000.
2. Write CTRL=1.
3. Read TIMER_V_LOWER0 about every 20*(P+1) cycles, at least 10 times (3 times for P=0xFFF), with i_d_ready=1. The values never come near a carry.
4. Write CTRL=0. Wait P+5 cycles after its D beat, then read TIMER_V_LOWER0 twice, 2*(P+1)+10 cycles apart.
5. Reprogram CFG0 for the next pair only after CTRL=0.
checks.expected:
Each read value v satisfies (v-V0) mod S = 0, and v=V0 when S=0. The values do not decrease.

For any two reads i<j with acceptance edges a_i, a_j and D-beat edges r_i, r_j, and S>0, n=(v_j-v_i)/S is an integer with floor((a_j-r_i)/(P+1)) <= n <= floor((r_j-a_i)/(P+1))+1.

The two reads after deactivation return the same value.

checks.title: Inactive after reset and first-tick latency
checks.behavior: The timer does not count while CTRL.active_0=0. The first tick comes no later than CFG0.prescale+1+4 cycles after the D beat of the activating write.
checks.stimulus:
After reset, read TIMER_V_LOWER0 at 10, 50 and 100 cycles. Then, for P in {0, 5, 47} with S=1:
1. With CTRL=0, write TIMER_V_LOWER0=0 and TIMER_V_UPPER0=0.
2. Write CTRL=1 (acceptance edge a0, D beat t0).
3. Issue a Get of TIMER_V_LOWER0 that is accepted at edge a with t0+P+6 <= a <= t0+P+10, and record its D-beat edge r.
4. Write CTRL=0.
checks.expected: The three reads after reset return 0. For each P, the read returns v >= 1 and v <= floor((r-a0)/(P+1))+1.

checks.title: Carry from lower to upper half and 64-bit compare
checks.behavior: Counting carries from TIMER_V_LOWER0 into TIMER_V_UPPER0. The compare uses all 64 bits, so a larger lower half with a smaller upper half does not raise the interrupt.
checks.stimulus:
Case A:
1. With CTRL=0, write CFG0=0x00010000 (P=0, S=1), TIMER_V_LOWER0=0xFFFFFFF0, TIMER_V_UPPER0=0x5, COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0x6, COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0x10 and INTR_ENABLE0=1.
2. Write CTRL=1 (acceptance edge a0, D beat t0).
3. Write CTRL=0 so that it is accepted between t0+40 and t0+100.
4. Wait 10 cycles and read TIMER_V_UPPER0 and TIMER_V_LOWER0.

Case B:
1. With CTRL=0, write CFG0=0x00300001 (P=1, S=0x30), TIMER_V_UPPER0=0 and TIMER_V_LOWER0=0xFFFFFFF0.
2. Activate for 50 cycles, deactivate, wait 10 cycles and read both halves.
checks.expected:
Case A:
- o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge before a0+31.
- o_intr_timer_expired=1 at some edge no later than t0+42 and stays 1.
- After deactivation, TIMER_V_UPPER0 reads 0x00000006 and 0x10 <= TIMER_V_LOWER0 <= 0x100.

Case B: with V=(UPPER<<32)|LOWER, V > 0xFFFFFFF0, (V-0xFFFFFFF0) mod 0x30 = 0 and TIMER_V_UPPER0=0x00000001.

checks.title: Behaviour near 2^64: wrap and intermediate interrupt
checks.behavior: mtime wraps modulo 2^64. With mtimecmp set to 2^64-step, the interrupt fires before the wrap and stays latched after it.
checks.stimulus:
Case A:
1. With CTRL=0, write CFG0=0x00030000 (P=0, S=3), TIMER_V_UPPER0=0xFFFFFFFF, TIMER_V_LOWER0=0xFFFFFFE0, COMPARE_UPPER0_0=0xFFFFFFFF, COMPARE_LOWER0_0=0xFFFFFFFD and INTR_ENABLE0=1.
2. Write CTRL=1 (acceptance edge a0, D beat t0).
3. Deactivate about 60 cycles later, wait 10 cycles, then read TIMER_V_UPPER0, TIMER_V_LOWER0 and INTR_STATE0.
4. Write INTR_STATE0=0x1 (D beat r), then read INTR_STATE0 at an edge >= r+4.

Case B:
1. With CTRL=0 and CFG0=0x00010000, write TIMER_V_UPPER0=0xFFFFFFFF and TIMER_V_LOWER0=0xFFFFFFFF.
2. Activate for 30 cycles, deactivate, wait 10 cycles and read both halves.
checks.expected:
Case A:
- o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge before a0+9.
- o_intr_timer_expired=1 at some edge no later than t0+20 and still 1 after the wrap.
- TIMER_V_UPPER0 reads 0x0, TIMER_V_LOWER0 < 0x100 and (TIMER_V_LOWER0+0x20) mod 3 = 0.
- INTR_STATE0 reads 0x1.
- After the W1C, INTR_STATE0 reads 0x0 and o_intr_timer_expired=0 at every edge >= r+6.

Case B: TIMER_V_UPPER0 reads 0x0 and TIMER_V_LOWER0 < 0x100.

checks.title: Outstanding requests and back-pressure
checks.behavior: Correct responses under pipelined requests, random o_a_ready stalls and random i_d_ready back-pressure. Responses are matched by d_source.
checks.stimulus: With CTRL=0, send 2000 random legal requests: full-word Get, PutFullData and PutPartialData (mask 1111) to CFG0, TIMER_V_LOWER0, TIMER_V_UPPER0, COMPARE_LOWER0_0, COMPARE_UPPER0_0 and INTR_ENABLE0, plus Gets to every mapped register. Allow up to 4 outstanding requests with distinct a_source values from 0 to 255. Assert i_a_valid without waiting for o_a_ready and hold the request until it is accepted. Drive i_d_ready randomly at 50%. Never have a write and another access to the same register outstanding at the same time.
checks.expected: Each accepted request gets exactly one response, matched by o_d_source, with o_d_error=0. Each read returns the reference model value, which is the last written data masked by the field mask (CFG0 0x00FF0FFF, INTR_ENABLE0 0x1, other registers 0xFFFFFFFF). Registers not written hold their reset values.

assumptions: Timing notation: 'edge' means a rising edge of clk_i. The acceptance edge of a request is the edge with i_a_valid=1 and o_a_ready=1. Its D beat (response edge) is the edge with o_d_valid=1, i_d_ready=1 and the matching o_d_source. 'N cycles after the write response' means N rising edges after that D beat.
The test bench changes inputs only immediately after rising edges of clk_i. Reset is released right after a rising edge.

The specification gives no latency for these events: IS_0 setting after an INTR_TEST0 write, IS_0 clearing by W1C when the condition is false, and the timer stopping after CTRL.active_0 is written 0. The plan uses the 4-cycle IS_0 bound of D-005/D-006 (plus 2 cycles for o_intr_timer_expired), and P+1+4 cycles for the timer to stop.
The D-013 text is cut off after 'Reads of any size'. Per RG-T1.4.1-07/08, aligned sub-word Gets whose mask is exactly the active lanes are taken to return the full register word with d_error=0.

A Get whose mask has bits outside its active lanes, and a PutFullData with a_size=2 and an incomplete mask, are taken to be d_error=1 cases (TL-T3.1.3.5-03/04, RT-4.1-06). For these and for undefined opcodes, only the response is checked, not register side effects.

IS_0 is a latched event (CP-T1.8.6-06). Only W1C to INTR_STATE0, writes to COMPARE_LOWER0_0 or COMPARE_UPPER0_0 (RT-T4.4-03/D-006), or reset clear it. Writing TIMER_V_* or CTRL does not clear it, and it stays 1 after mtime wraps below mtimecmp.
The generic comportability offsets and order for INTR_STATE, INTR_ENABLE and INTR_TEST (0x0, 0x4, 0x8) are overridden by the rv_timer register table (0x100 ENABLE, 0x104 STATE, 0x108 TEST).
The byte writes of D-013 are issued as PutPartialData with a_size=0 and mask 0001.
A tick cannot occur before the edge at which the activating CTRL write is accepted. This gives the lower bounds on interrupt timing and on tick counts.

decisions.question: Are Status interrupts' INTR_STATE bits ro mirroring the input, and does INTR_TEST apply to Status type? The quote only says INTR_STATE is ro for Status.
decisions.answer: Out of scope: rv_timer has only an Event-type interrupt (spec D-019). Status-type behaviour is not checked. Delegated decision, not a hardware designer's review.

decisions.question: Can fatal cause registers be reset by system reset? 'Not clearable in any way' needs an exception for reset.
decisions.answer: rv_timer has no cause register for its fatal alert, so this is not checked. A reset ends the repeated fatal alert (comportability: fatal alerts repeat until reset; spec D-010). Delegated decision, not a hardware designer's review.

decisions.question: Is 'wait 2 cycles between handshakes' measured from ack deassertion to next alert assertion, and is it exact or a minimum?
decisions.answer: Neither the start point nor exactness is checked. Only the bounds of spec D-009 and D-010 are checked: first pulse within 16 cycles, then at least one pulse every 32 cycles while the fatal alert lasts. Delegated decision, not a hardware designer's review.
